description: per-family coupling contrast index versus per-family GCP-GAP gain
_t_interval_omitted: No Student-t interval is reported. These quantities are Pearson and Spearman correlations computed once over 15 attack-family units (11 in the restricted variant). There is no n=5 seed sample and no mean, so defect 2.2 of notes/20260720-bug-prepublication-code-audit.md does not describe them and a t interval for a mean is undefined for a correlation. The honest uncertainty statement is a resampling interval over the family units, which is what this file reports. The file is therefore named *_ci.json and not *_tci.json, so the name does not promise an interval the file does not contain
_fisher_z_caveat: fisher_z_ci assumes the units are independent draws from a bivariate normal. These 15 families are not: they are pooled across two datasets (9 from NF-ToN-IoT-v2, 6 from NF-CSE-CIC-IDS2018-v2), families within a dataset share one trained model pair and one feature encoding, and the gcp_gain values are seed-averaged rather than single draws. Read it as a second opinion on the bootstrap, not as a coverage guarantee
_interval_method: percentile bootstrap over the attack-family units, 10,000 resamples, percentiles 2.5 and 97.5, RNG seed 20260711 (the seed the published pearson_ci95 used). Student-t for a mean is deliberately NOT applied here
_reason: scripts/recompute_t_intervals.py did not reach results/efc. The quantities here are correlations, not means, so they get a bootstrap-over-families interval rather than a Student-t interval
